newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong to export gasoline to Aramco.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong to export gasoline to Aramco.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Oil Refining Co said on Friday it had signed an agreement to export 1.8 million barrels of gasoline to Saudi Arabia's state-oil company Saudi Aramco over six months. The deal is Ssangyong's first long-term contract to export gasoline, a company spokesman said.
The first shipment of 300,000 barrels would be made this month, he said.
"The first delivery is expected to be made around July 20," the spokesman said.
He said the export price would fluctuate in accordance with Singapore spot prices.
"The startup of our new residue fluid catalytic cracker (RFCC) in April enabled us to sign the first-ever long-term gasoline export deal," he said.
The new RFCC has a 50,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) capacity.
He said the gasoline would contain low sulphur, low benzene and an octane level of 95.
Ssangyong, which has a total refining capacity of 443,000 bpd, is South Korea's third largest refiner.
The buyer, Saudi Aramco, owns 35 percent of the refiner and provides the bulk of Ssangyong's crude requirements.
The spokesman said the agreement was also South Korea's first term contract to sell gasoline to an oil-producing country.
